selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the main point of the passage about one apple?
questions.answer: Even one apple shows that its true Giver must be the Creator Who controls the whole world.

questions.question: Which big things are mentioned as being under Allah’s control in order for fruit to reach people?
questions.answer: The seasons, the day and night cycle, and the turning of the earth are mentioned.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect a single apple to the whole earth?
questions.answer: Because the apple depends on a huge system in the world, not just on itself alone.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying the earth is like a garden for the apple?
questions.answer: It means the earth is the wide place where the apple and other living things are grown and cared for.

questions.question: What does the passage compare the universe to when speaking about where the apple is produced?
questions.answer: It compares the universe to a tree and to a book.

questions.question: How do spring and summer help in the example?
questions.answer: They are shown as the times when the fruit grows and becomes ready.

questions.question: What idea is taught by saying the same mark is found on all fruits, plants, and animals?
questions.answer: It teaches that they all come from the same Maker.

questions.question: Who is described as the true Owner and Maker of the apple?
questions.answer: The majestic and beautiful Creator of all living things and of the whole world.

questions.question: What does it mean that every fruit is a “seal of unity”?
questions.answer: Each fruit points to one Creator and is a sign that creation comes from Him alone.

questions.question: How does the last sentence strengthen the message of Allah’s oneness?
questions.answer: It says that every fruit gives its own witness, so the signs of unity are many and repeated.

questions.question: According to the passage, can an apple be explained by a small, separate cause only?
questions.answer: No. It needs the work of the One Who runs the whole universe.

questions.question: Why are the changing seasons important in the argument?
questions.answer: They help bring different foods at the right times, showing wise planning.

questions.question: What picture is given of the earth when people receive fruits from it?
questions.answer: The earth is pictured like a ship carrying goods to needy guests.

questions.question: What does the passage say can be seen on the apple itself?
questions.answer: It says there are signs of wise design, mercy, and neediness on it.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention other apples, fruits, plants, and animals too?
questions.answer: To show that the same kind of sign appears on all of them, so they have one Maker.

questions.question: If one Being made the apple, what else must also belong to Him according to the passage?
questions.answer: The earth, the seasons, the larger world, and the creatures connected with the apple must also belong to Him.

questions.question: What relationship does the passage give between the apple and other creatures in the world?
questions.answer: It says they are like its companions and related fellow-creatures.

questions.question: What is meant by calling fruit a “seal”?
questions.answer: It means fruit is like a mark of ownership that points to its true Maker.

questions.question: What is the main lesson a student should take from the whole passage?
questions.answer: Small blessings like fruit should lead us to recognize Allah’s power, wisdom, mercy, and oneness.

questions.question: In the final idea of the passage, what does every fruit announce?
questions.answer: Every fruit announces Allah’s unity and points back to Him.

questions.question: What everyday object is used in the passage to teach a big truth?
questions.answer: An apple is used.

questions.question: What big truth does the apple teach?
questions.answer: It teaches that Allah alone is the Maker and Provider.

questions.question: Why does the passage speak about night and day turning one after another?
questions.answer: To show that even the giving of fruit depends on the order of the whole world.

questions.question: How is the earth described in a way that sounds like travel and delivery?
questions.answer: It is described like a loaded ship bringing food to those who need it.
